text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The annual Rock Summer festival was a failure as the daily turnout was only 2-3,000 instead of an estimated 12-15,000. Organiser Juri Makarov said he will not hold a festival next year.

- Thirty-two literary figures have protested against the celebration of former Language and Literature Institute director Endel Sogel's birthday in a literature and culture centre. Sogel is suspected of having participated in deportations in 1941 and of persecution of intellectuals during the Soviet regime.
- The Estonia Theatre ended its season on Sunday with 225th performance.
- The Estonian consulate in Moscow expects a rise of visa applications for the summer.
- The government institutions' press representatives left yesterday for a week-long study tour in Germany.
- More than 5,000 participants of the youth song and dance festival will arrive in Tallinn today. The festival will take place next weekend.

- Swedish journalist Elisabeth Crona replied to Foreign Minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves, who accused her of having inaccurately described a meeting with Russian journalists. The article claimed that Ilves had answered the Russians' provocative questions with insults.
- The school computerisation programme, dubbed Tiger's Leap by the president, will finance 11 educational software projects this year.

- The Tallinn city government has banned securities transactions by the municipal water works. The company had sold two million kroons worth of Tallinna Pank shares and lost 800,000 kroons on the deal.
- A rape oil factory is to be founded in the central Estonian town of Paunkula. The plant is expected to begin operations next year.
- An insurance firm intends to build a 12-storey office block near the Stockmann department store in Tallinn.
